slides.lead: Memes, sounds and scenes in real time – triggered by what the creator says. In under a second, hands-free, on TikTok LIVE, Instagram, YouTube and Twitch.
slides.vision: And tomorrow: You talk. It becomes a scene.
slides.name: Tuncay Sancak
slides.contact: Investor Relations: Gönül Demet  ·  [Email]  ·  October 2026  ·  Confidential
slides.notes: Quick intro: I stream myself, I write books, and I built LiveFX because my live streams were missing exactly what every short video has. What you see today runs in my own streams. At the end I'll show where this is going: from a meme overlay to a visual language for everything spoken. Thirty seconds, then straight to the problem.

slides.title: Live is raw. The edit comes too late.
rows: Everything that makes short videos go viral happens afterwards
Memes, sounds, zooms, stickers – added in the edit, after recording. Live, you get none of it.
The creator is host, director and editor at once
With two hands, one camera and a chat that won't wait.
Existing tools react to viewers or to keys
Alerts for donations and follows, soundboards on hotkeys. Both need a click.
slides.callout: Nobody reacts to the spoken word.
slides.calloutSub: Auto-captions proved it: real-time text from speech works. Real-time effects from speech don't exist yet.
slides.quote: “I say ‘wild’ – and nothing happens, except me reaching for the keyboard.”  – Tuncay Sancak, from his own stream
slides.notes: Auto-captions proved that real-time text from speech works – and that platforms build it in natively. Real-time effects from speech don't exist. That's exactly the gap we fill. An example from my stream: I say “wild” – and nothing happens, except me reaching for the keyboard.

slides.title: Voice → effect in under a second
facts: < 1 s reaction – matches fire on interim recognition results
Hands-free – no key, no click, no second monitor
Runs locally on the creator's own computer – privacy built in
AI mode (optional) catches sentences without a keyword: “that was so embarrassing” → Awkward
slides.notes: Key point: keyword matching is instant (it works on interim recognition results) and needs no cloud. The optional AI mode catches sentences without a keyword (“that was so embarrassing for him” → Awkward). Everything runs on the creator's own computer – privacy is built in, not bolted on.

The line that sticks: the first video in which memes reacted to my voice convinced me more than any slide.

13 full-screen scenes, 12 ambience loops, story packs DE/TR/EN
Türkçe 85 · Deutsch 49 · English 50 · Family & Kids 27 · Gaming 27 – plus GIF search
38 synthesized sounds (no license fees), mixer with limiter, ducking, stereo, reverb
Twitch chat, YouTube chat, gift webhook (TikTok via TikFinity / Streamer.bot)
Phone remote (PWA), OBS/Streamlabs, TikTok LIVE Studio, IG Live Producer, demo without OBS

slides.notes: This is no longer a prototype: releases from 0.1 to 2.0, unit and end-to-end tests, guides in German and Turkish. Version 2.0 was a hardening release for stage use and sales. Stress two things: (1) our own sounds and packs mean no copyright strikes, (2) viewer triggers are the bridge to monetization – a gift can already trigger an effect today.

creators went live on TikTok in 2025 in Southeast Asia, the Caucasus and Central Asia alone, +77% [Source 2]
of the creator economy (~$216–260B in 2026) is live [Source 3, 4]
cards: Live commerce and gifting (TikTok LIVE, IG Badges, Super Chat) turn live into a business – not a side format.
Streaming ASR < 300 ms, models in the browser, WebGPU in all major browsers [Source 27], AI classification for < $1/hour.
CapCut ↔ TikTok, Edits ↔ Instagram. Live tools are the next step – and nobody has voice-driven effects.
slides.notes: Live is no longer a side channel – it's a revenue channel. And Turkey is a young, meme-loving TikTok market with hardly any localized tools – our biggest pack is the Turkish one, and that's no accident. Tech: what needed a server three years ago now runs in the browser – and that's also the foundation of the vision from slide 12 on.

slides.title: Live video from words: You talk. It becomes a scene.
pipeline: Mic, reading aloud or a finished video file
World state ≤ 1 KB, one shared timeline
Drawn in the browser, 60 fps, on your own device
lines: Every sentence grows a continuous picture-book film – below or beside the live image.
Spoken word → picture, the word in the target language and its pronunciation. Learning and reading aid.
Stage, classroom, audiobook with pictures, AR on the phone, VR and display glasses.
Live editor and auto-edit: video in, fully edited out – no upload.
today: Voice becomes a meme, sound or scene in under a second – in use in the founder's own streams.
tomorrow: Voice becomes a film, a word picture with pronunciation or a finished clip – on stream, in school, on stage, in your glasses.
slides.tagline: Draw, don't generate – on the compute budget of a caption, not a data center.
slides.notes: Live captions showed that platforms want to process speech in real time – for free, on billions of devices. We're the next step: pictures instead of text. One engine, one timeline, four lines: Story Film, WortBild, Spaces, Studio. Everything runs in the browser on your own device: a sentence becomes a state delta of a few hundred bytes, drawn in a single canvas. No video diffusion model, no GPU server. To be honest: this is the vision for 2027–2029 – hence the badge. It builds on code that already runs today (story mode, effect engine, offline recognition). WebGPU is now available in all major browsers [Source 27] – we only use it optionally.

slides.title: Generative Scene Engine: live video from words

scene.transcript: “It was night … a girl walked into the forest … it started to rain … suddenly, a dragon!”

cost.title: Cost per hour of companion video
cost.scale: log scale · video AI at list price $0.05–0.75/s [Source 24, 25] · LiveFX AI cost: project measurement

slides.rolesTitle: Every sentence changes the world state:
bullets: The streamer reads aloud or tells a story – below, an animated film builds sentence by sentence: night, forest, rain, dragon.
Runs at 60 fps in the browser next to OBS, offline and deterministic: same timeline, same picture – every story instantly becomes a clip.
240 to over 10,000 times cheaper than video AI – and the only way to do it live.
For read-aloud, audiobook and podcast formats: German audiobooks €374M, +13% [Source 19]; YouTube > 1B podcast viewers a month [Source 21].
honest: Picture book on purpose, not photorealism
A stylized world of emoji/SVG and particles – which is exactly why it's live, cheap and child-friendly. Optional AI only picks the scene; it never generates images.
slides.notes: Here's how it looks: the streamer does nothing but talk. “It was night” – the sky goes dark. “A girl walked into the forest” – trees grow, the character walks in. “It started to rain” – rain, the ambience loop switches. “Suddenly, a dragon” – lightning, a camera jolt, the dragon. Technically: one sentence produces a delta of 200–500 bytes, scenes change 1 to 3 times a minute, and everything is drawn in one canvas with at most 1,200 particles – a budget our effect engine already handles next to OBS today. Cost: at list price, video AI costs $0.05 (Veo 3.1 Lite, 720p) to $0.75 per second [Source 24, 25] – $180–2,700 per hour, and it can't run live at all. LiveFX: €0 without AI, $0.25–0.75 per hour with optional text AI. Market: German audiobooks €374M [Source 19], 23.8M people in Germany listen to podcasts weekly [Source 20], YouTube has over 1B podcast viewers [Source 21]; AI video grows from $3.67B to $24.89B by 2036 [Source 23]. Timeline: German MVP in Q2 2027, TR/EN and world packs in Q3 2027. First publisher case: the founder's own children's book series.

slides.title: Language learning & education: every word a picture
bullets: A child says “apple” – instantly: 🍎, “elma” in the target language, “der Apfel” with a color-coded article, and the pronunciation. No click.
Reading aid in your own language: for pre-readers, German as a second language, integration courses and neurodivergent learners.
Local, no account, offline – school-grade privacy as a selling point. Pronunciation via the device's system voices [Source 29].
slides.revenue: Revenue (estimate): WortBild Family €4.99/month · school license €300–800/year · course license €49 per teacher per year · publisher edition for bilingual books
slides.notes: The most personal part: I write children's books about neurodiversity, and I'm German-Turkish. The teacher sets three things – “I speak: German”, “Show: Türkçe”, and the mode – and reads aloud. Every word from the learning list becomes picture, word and pronunciation. Repeat-after-me is deliberately not pronunciation scoring, just a green check mark. Tech: word → picture is a table lookup, the operating system provides the pronunciation (speechSynthesis) [Source 29], a school tablet is enough, server cost per child: zero. Market: Duolingo has 58.7M daily users and 12.7M paying subscribers [Source 32], language-learning apps make $1.54B in-app [Source 33], 20.4% of pupils under 16 in Germany mainly speak another language at home [Source 37], 2.65M people in Germany have a migration background from Turkey [Source 38], 25% of fourth-graders fall below the minimum reading standard [Source 39]. Price anchor: ANTON school license €250–700 [Source 41]. Honestly: integration is small in euro terms; it brings credibility and funding. The volume lies with families, publishers and platforms. We say “supports vocabulary learning”, not “twice as fast”.

slides.title: Auto-edit, editor, VR/AR – and a bigger market
slides.studioTitle: LiveFX Studio: live editing and auto-edit
studioItems: After the stream, 3–5 clips in 9:16 – where memes, gifts and chat were densest. No upload.
Drop a video → local transcript → effects, scenes, cuts as chips → MP4 via hardware encoder [Source 57, 59].
slides.roomsTitle: LiveFX Spaces: one state, many screens

market.title: Expanded market
market.note: Price anchors: OpusClip $15–29, Descript $16–65 per month [Source 54, 55]. LiveFX Pro+ €14.99 (estimate) – no cloud costs, no minute caps. XR and glasses: a showcase, not a revenue line.

slides.notes: Two doors into the same tool. First, live → highlights: our server already knows every trigger, every gift and every chat message with a timestamp – that yields 3–5 clips per stream. Second, auto-edit: drag a 20-minute MP4 into the window, Whisper transcribes it locally in the browser [Source 60], LiveFX places effects, scenes and cuts as movable chips, and export runs through WebCodecs and the device's hardware encoder [Source 57, 58, 59]. The file never leaves the computer; the marginal cost per video is zero. Spaces: stage and classroom already work today (full screen, phone as the control desk). Audiobook with pictures and AR on the phone come in 2027. WebXR [Source 47, 48] and display glasses like Meta Ray-Ban Display [Source 46] are vision – IDC expects 13.6M smart glasses in 2026 [Source 45], and display glasses are only a small share of that. Competition, honestly: CapCut has 736M MAU [Source 52]; we're not competing as a universal editor but through voice → effect, scenes, TR/DE and local processing. Buyer signal: in 2026 Canva acquired Cavalry and MangoAI [Source 56].
